response: The clinically positive axilla in breast cancer is not necessarily a contraindication to sentinel lymph node biopsy. Clinical axillary examination can yield false-positive results and is insufficient on its own to justify axillary lymph node dissection. If other preoperative assessments, such as palpation- or image-guided fine needle aspiration, are negative or indeterminate, then sentinel lymph node biopsy may be considered as an alternative to routine axillary lymph node dissection, even in cases with a clinically positive axilla. This approach can help avoid unnecessary lymph node dissection and its associated complications.
